news.title: Infantino could earn millions with World Cup stake sales as UEFA issue statement
news.lede: The FIFA president has spent a decade at the top of football's global governing body but looks set to cash in on it's biggest tournament. According to The Times, he plans to market stakes in the World Cup to private investors. This would lead to the introduction of a new company that will be in charge of top competitions across men's and women's football. The World Cup and Club World Cup would also come under control, and therefore expansion or more regular editions could materialise.

news.title: World Cup: UEFA hit out at FIFA and Gianni Infantino amid plans to sell minority stakes linked to competition
news.lede: UEFA have hit out at FIFA's plans to sell stakes linked to the World Cup to private investors. On Tuesday, FIFA released a detailed statement outlining plans to launch a new commercial company as it targets $10bn-plus (£7.5bn) development funding. FIFA says it could deliver more than $10bn in football development funding over the next four years through the creation of a new commercial subsidiary, subject to approval from its member associations. FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a FIFA-owned company, would bring together its commercial rights, including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing, alongside the operational delivery of FIFA tournaments.

news.title: Infantino reportedly plans to sell World Cup shares to investors
news.lede: On Tuesday afternoon, several well-informed journalists revealed that FIFA would soon announce plans to sell shares in the World Cup. It didn’t take long - within two hours, FIFA issued an official statement confirming the intentions described in Martyn Ziegler’s explosive article for The Times. Currently, the World Cup is organised solely by FIFA as an independent body governing global football. Under the new vision, FIFA would create a separate company to manage the tournament (FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE for short), and minority shares in it would be sold.

news.title: FIFA plan for Kushner-backed USD 20 billion operation to run FIFA World Cup meets fury from Europe’s UEFA
news.lede: AFP AFP https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/6aal43/article71278206.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/image%2097.jpg NEW YORK The governing body of world football is collaborating with JPMorgan to attract external investors, potentially offering up to a 20 percent stake in this venture. FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s plan to create a USD 20 billion company running the FIFA World Cup with private investors including the Kushner family was announced Tuesday — and immediately attacked by European football body UEFA. “It is not FIFA’s to sell,” UEFA said in a statement. “None of us are the owners of football.”

news.title: Stunning surprise: FIFA wants to sell the World Cup and UEFA responds with a fiery statement
news.lede: What does Trump have to do with the crisis? A major crisis has erupted between world football's governing body, FIFA, and its European counterpart, UEFA, days after Spain lifted the 2026 World Cup. According to "The Times" newspaper, FIFA president Gianni Infantino intends to sell the World Cup in the form of shares to private-sector investors, taking on a role similar to a commissioner in this new project. The Times reported that Infantino's idea has provoked a furious reaction from the Union of European Football Associations.

news.title: UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words
news.lede: UEFA have taken aim at FIFA and said that football is ‘not theirs to sell’ in the face of their outrageous plan. Recent reports have suggested that world football’s governing body is planning on selling stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The scheme could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn millions if a deal is rubber-stamped. The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted.
